results.rationale: Consistency: The tan coat, green backdrop and sandy setting remain recognizable, but the face/eye shape, head position, tail curve and background/ground texture change. Anatomical repair is excluded from this assessment. Instruction: The legs are repositioned and the leftmost paw is lifted; a corrected puppy should have four coherent limbs. Five separate legs and paws remain, so the central anatomical defect is largely uncorrected. Quality alone: Structural coherence is problematic because of the extra foreleg; fur also has conspicuous combed, repetitive ridging. Lighting and setting are coherent.

Consistency: The tan puppy and outdoor composition remain, but the muzzle/eyes, ear contours, tail position and ground texture noticeably change beyond anatomical correction. Instruction: The splayed leg becomes more upright and the inner paw moves backward. The expected result is four normally attached limbs; a duplicate leg and paw remain immediately behind the left foreground leg, leaving five paws. Most of the essential correction is missing. Quality alone: Natural light, fur and background are satisfactory, but the duplicated left foreleg/paw is a clear anatomical artifact.

Consistency: The puppy identity is substantially changed to a broad-headed, heavier dog with amber eyes, a dark muzzle and altered ears; body proportions and background texture also change. The green-and-sand scene remains. Instruction: The extra foreground limb is removed and a coherent four-legged stance is established. A perfect result would repair the same puppy; this instead substantially replaces its appearance with a mature-looking dog, so compliance is partial. Quality alone: Anatomy, four-leg arrangement, paw contact, lighting and fur texture are coherent, with no noticeable generation artifacts.

Consistency: The tan puppy and general scene layout remain, but the muzzle markings, facial contours, tail curve and background/ground texture visibly change. Requested limb corrections are excluded. Instruction: The extra foreleg is removed and the puppy now has a plausible four-legged arrangement, with the far hind paw partly occluded. The left foreground paw still has irregular merged toes and an awkward wrist contour, so the repair has a minor residual defect. Quality alone: Lighting and overall form are natural, but the left foreground paw has distorted toe outlines and a conspicuous uneven transition at the wrist; the remaining fur and setting are coherent.
